_readme: ⭐⭐⭐ ORDENCE — THE SCHEDULER CLOCK. Wave 14, Track A.
This is the config for a SECOND Railway service in the SAME project and the
SAME repository as the web service. It is not read by the web service; point
the new service's Config-as-code path at this file (Settings → Config as code
→ railway.cron.json), or set RAILWAY_CONFIG_FILE=railway.cron.json on it.
🔴 DO NOT PUT A CRON SCHEDULE ON THE WEB SERVICE. Railway's cron feature
RESTARTS a service on a schedule, so attaching it to a service that never
exits restarts the website every five minutes. And a scaled web tier runs N
replicas: a scheduler inside it fires every job once per replica, which for
dunning means two statutory demand notices at two serial numbers. The ledger
claim in SQL-FILES/0129 would refuse the second one, but a design that leans
on its last line of defence every night is not a design.
🔴 WHY buildCommand IS `echo`, AND WHY THAT IS NOT LAZINESS.
The clock needs `node`, `node_modules` and two .mjs files. It does NOT need a
Next.js production bundle, and building one here would double every deploy,
double the memory ceiling, and make the scheduler fail to deploy for reasons
that have nothing to do with scheduling. RAILPACK still installs dependencies
before the build command runs, so `@neondatabase/serverless` is present.
⚠️ startCommand RUNS `node` DIRECTLY BECAUSE package.json IS SHARED AND
OWNED BY NOBODY THIS WAVE. An `npm run scheduler:tick` script would be the
tidier form; it is in PATCH-REQUEST-A.md.
⚠️ EVERY FIVE MINUTES, ONE LINE, FOREVER. The clock does not know what the
jobs are — it POSTs {"mode":"tick"} and the application answers from
server/scheduler/catalog.ts. That is what keeps every cadence in the
repository instead of in this console, and it is why adding a ninth job
schedules it by the commit that adds it rather than by somebody remembering
to come back here.
VARIABLES THIS SERVICE NEEDS (Railway → the cron service → Variables):
WORKER_API_SECRET        ⭐ ALREADY SET on the live Railway service —
measured from the deployment. Somebody prepared
for scheduled work and nothing ever called it.
Use that existing value; do NOT mint a new name.
Railway shares project variables across services,
so the cron service may already see it.
With no secret set /api/workers answers 503 and
refuses to run anything, which is deliberate.
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL      Already catalogued and already set. Read as the
default address of the web service.
SCHEDULER_APP_URL        OPTIONAL, and the ONLY new required-ish name.
Overrides NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL — set it when the
cron service should reach the web service over
Railway private networking instead of the public
hostname.
MAINTENANCE_DATABASE_URL OPTIONAL. A connection string for the
ordence_maintenance role. Without it the four
retention jobs — prune_change_log,
prune_security_events, prune_usage_counters and
prune_scheduler_runs — do not run, and the
watchdog reports them overdue rather than letting
the silence pass unnoticed. See SQL-FILES/0132
Section 6 for how to create the role.
⚠️ CRON_SECRET IS ALSO ALREADY SET ON THE LIVE SERVICE AND IS DELIBERATELY
NOT READ HERE. It belongs to /api/cron/canary, whose response names real
workspace ids and must not be reachable with the token a cron runner holds
for everything else. The canary now runs as the `rls_canary` job INSIDE the
application — server/scheduler/catalog.ts calls runCanaryProbe() directly —
so this process never needs a second secret. Two secrets for one job is how
a scheduler authenticates against the wrong one at 3am.
⚠️ ORDENCE_INLINE_JOBS IS SET ON PRODUCTION, AND ITS DEFAULT IS ON ANYWAY.
isInlineFallbackEnabled() reads `?? "1"`, so with no Cloudflare queue bound
— and Railway binds none — every enqueueJob() call runs its processor INLINE,
inside the request. For the scheduler that means the tick performs the
contract expiry scan itself rather than handing it to a queue, so the job's
declared budget governs real work and the response reports via:"inline".
That is correct and visible; see TRACK-REPORT-WAVE-17.md §3 for the
double-execution analysis it prompted.
🔴 THE SCHEDULER IS NOT THE ALARM. If this service is deleted, misconfigured
or silently stops, nothing here will tell you. Point an external uptime
monitor at
GET https://app.ordence.com/api/workers?watchdog=1
Authorization: Bearer $WORKER_API_SECRET
It answers 200 when every declared job has completed inside its declared
window and the clock is beating, and 503 when it has not. Nothing about that
answer is computed by this service, which is the entire point: the failure
this product has actually had for years is the scheduler not existing.

build.buildCommand: echo 'scheduler clock: no build step — see _readme in railway.cron.json'
